Lesson · 25 min

Join and Take Part in a Google Meet Call

Join Google Meet calls from Calendar, a link, or a code; check your camera and microphone; use captions, chat, reactions, and raise hand; present a tab or window; and leave cleanly.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Join a Google Meet call from Google Calendar, a link, or a meeting code
  • ✓Check your microphone, camera, and visual effects before you join
  • ✓Use captions, chat, reactions, and raise hand during a call
  • ✓Present a tab, a window, or your entire screen, and stop presenting
  • ✓Change the layout, find Meeting tools, explain when recording is available, and leave the call

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Join a call

On the job

You join Parkview's weekly leasing huddle from a busy front office.

The huddle starts in two minutes. Coworkers are talking behind you, Andre will ask you about the showing calendar, and Denise wants you to share the lease renewal slides.

Your task: Join on time, sound and look professional, take part without interrupting, and share only what you mean to share.

You see a preview screen before you join. If you're on the invitation and signed in, select Join now. If you aren't on the invitation, or you aren't signed in to a Google Account, select Ask to join; someone in the meeting has to let you in.

Before you join

  • Use the microphone and camera buttons on the preview to turn each one on or off. A red button means it's off.
  • Select Apply visual effects to blur your background or choose a background image, which hides a busy office or a home.
  • Use More options › Settings to pick a different microphone, speaker, or camera, and to test your speakers.
  • Then select Join now (or Ask to join).
💡 Join with your microphone off in a noisy place, and turn it on when you speak. Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + D turns the microphone on or off and Ctrl + E does the same for the camera.

During the call

Select Chat at the bottom right to send messages to everyone in the call. Unless your organization uses continuous meeting chat, people who join late don't see earlier messages, and the messages disappear when the call ends, so don't put anything there that needs to be kept.

Drag and drop: match

Drag each card into place, or tap a card and then tap where it goes.

Present your screen

  1. Select Present now.
  2. Choose A tab, A window, or Your entire screen.
  3. Pick the tab or window and select Share.
  4. When you're done, select Stop presenting.

Presenting a tab shares that tab's sound too. For a window or your entire screen, turn on Also share system audio in the sharing window if people need to hear it. A meeting allows up to 10 presentations at the same time, and your organization's settings or the meeting host can turn presenting off.

Share a tab or a window, not your entire screen, whenever you can. Your entire screen shows everything, including email notifications and any tenant information that pops up.

Layouts, Meeting tools, and recording

To change how people appear, select More options › Change layout. Auto (dynamic) is the default and adjusts to the meeting. Tiled (legacy) shows people in a grid. Spotlight fills the window with the speaker or the presentation. Sidebar shows the speaker or presentation large with others at the side.

Meeting tools at the bottom right holds features such as Recording. Recording is only available with certain Google Workspace editions (and Google One plans with 2 TB or more), and an administrator has to allow it; a free personal account can't record. When a meeting is recorded, the recording is saved to the organizer's Google Drive in a Google Meet folder.

If you use Microsoft Teams, the ideas carry over: Teams also has raise hand, reactions, live captions, chat, and sharing a window or screen.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Try Google Meet with your own Google Account.

  1. Go to meet.google.com, select New meeting, then Start an instant meeting. (You'll be the only one in it.)
  2. Turn your microphone off and on, and blur your background with Apply visual effects or More options.
  3. Turn on captions and say a sentence to see them appear.
  4. Select Present now › A tab and share any tab. Then select Stop presenting.
  5. Change the layout to Spotlight, take a screenshot, and leave the call.
Deliverable: Submit your screenshot and one sentence about which Meet control you'll use most at work. If you can't use a camera or Meet on your computer, complete the practice simulations and submit their results pages.
